A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Contrastive Sparse Representation (CSR) work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–E are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet, text, and multimodal experiments, including retrieval measurements and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds matched-backbone ImageNet evaluations, zero-shot multimodal retrieval, and multiplication-count analysis.

M1.justification: Both versions use frozen embeddings, a TopK sparse autoencoder, auxiliary and Multi-TopK reconstruction losses, and a contrastive objective. v3 explicitly writes ReLU after TopK, clarifying the nonnegative latents already assumed in v1; this does not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds CC3M training and zero-shot transfer to MS COCO and Flickr30K, substantially extending evaluation beyond target-dataset training in the multimodal experiments. Existing ImageNet and text coverage remains. Appendix B.1 mentions few-shot results, but no separately identifiable outcomes support counting additional few-shot coverage.

E2.justification: MRL-LP enters the linear-probing accuracy comparison in v3 Figure 7(a) and Table 5, whereas v1 included it only in Figure 1(c)'s training-cost comparison; it disappears from that revised cost plot. The text and multimodal comparator sets remain unchanged after matching shortened model names.

E3.justification: v3 adds ImageNet comparisons using the FF2048 ResNet50 backbone alongside the retained stronger-backbone results, and adds linear-probing evaluation. Table 3 changes the reported image-training batch size from 1024 to 4096 and gamma from 1.0 to 0.1. Appendix D introduces separate CC3M training protocols for zero-shot evaluation. These are substantive experimental-setting changes, without establishing that every retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: The new CC3M-to-COCO/Flickr30K evaluation tests cross-dataset multimodal generalization. Appendix E.4 and Table 11 additionally test the runtime explanation by counting multiplications across hidden dimensions and sparsity levels. Existing backbone-size, hidden-dimension, loss, and dead-latent analyses in Figures 4–6 and 8 are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three random seeds and mean performance for the Appendix E.1–E.2 studies. They also retain the same 2000 timing rounds and 100 warm-up rounds in E.3. No new uncertainty-reporting practice or significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial matched-backbone, linear-probing, zero-shot retrieval, and operation-count results. In Table 4, v1's CSR accuracy of 73.84 at eight active dimensions remains under the stronger-backbone label; the new FF2048 result is 67.78, not a same-setting deterioration. Retained entries also change: CSR's NFCorpus score rises from 37.06 to 38.06 in Table 1, and several stronger-backbone ImageNet scores are revised. Table 2's existing in-distribution scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The objectives and cited NCL identifiability theorem retain their mathematical substance, with no new proof or formal guarantee. Explicit ReLU notation clarifies existing nonnegativity. The removed Johnson–Lindenstrauss analogy and added runtime explanation are informal interpretations rather than formal derivations.

C1.justification: The central sparse-compression contribution and broad efficiency claims remain. The introduction reduces the stated ImageNet advantage from 17% to 9% and replaces the claim that MRL requires training from scratch with a requirement for full-parameter updates. The conclusion additionally claims complementarity with other acceleration techniques.

C2.justification: v3 gives more specific backend and nonzero-overlap explanations for sparse retrieval speed, removes the Johnson–Lindenstrauss analogy, and interprets the new zero-shot results as evidence of scalability and transfer. The dead-latent limitation already appeared in v1. Some overgeneralization remains: Figure 7's all-dimensions superiority wording conflicts with Table 5 at larger dimensions.

D1.justification: v3 identifies FF2048, explains SVD and random-feature baseline construction, specifies Figure 1(c)'s averaging range, and adds CC3M hyperparameters and trainable-parameter counts. It removes v1's sentence-transformer implementation note for Int8 quantization. Hardware, core code-access information, and most existing implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The sparse-coding discussion adds Gamma-prior models and concept bottlenecks, and the conclusion relates CSR to pruning, quantization, and distillation. SAE background gains the k-sparse autoencoder citation. Duan et al. (2024) changes from Contrastive Factor Analysis to A Non-negative VAE, while several earlier citations are removed. The overall MRL-versus-sparse-coding positioning remains.

P1.justification: Sections 3.2 and 4 undergo extensive explanatory rewriting, including renamed method subsections and a reorganized timing discussion. Section 5 gains a baseline-description paragraph and substantially revised analyses, while the conclusion becomes Conclusion & Discussion. These changes exceed local copyediting despite retaining the overall section and appendix organization.

P2.justification: Figures 1, 3, and 7 are substantially revised, including backbone distinctions, timing axes, and replacement of Figure 7's retrieval-time panel with linear-probing results. Table 2 expands to full width with zero-shot and parameter columns; Table 4 separates backbone settings; Tables 5 and 11 are added. Table 1 gains method categories, while Figures 4–6 and 8 retain their plotted content.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses an important weakness in v1's central ImageNet comparison: CSR's stronger pretrained backbone confounded attribution of its advantage. The FF2048 comparisons and separate stronger-backbone columns make the method's contribution substantially more assessable. Zero-shot multimodal experiments and operation-count analysis further strengthen generalization and efficiency evidence. Blanket superiority wording still conflicts with some linear-probing results, but the improved controls and supporting analyses provide a substantial net gain in credibility.
